doc.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002

title: Jazz is not about the money
summary: Money should not be the criterion; some of his best playing was free gigs with Bill Holman.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Well it’s good to have your priorities in order, it’s very important.

It’s not about the bread. Everything can’t be about the money, it just can’t, especially not this, not the craft, not what you do, you can’t be about the bread. Yes you want to make it. Yes you want to be successful. But I’ll be damned if your criteria is how much money you make, you will not play the same. Some of the best playing I’ve ever done is gigs for free with Bill Holman in LA, or where you’re working for the door and you made seven bucks. That’s some of the best playing you did for twelve people. Something like that, where you broke these things and played wonderful. In the rehearsal room with Bill one day I remember flipping everybody out in a couple of solos on “Blue Daniel” and something else. Knocked everybody out. There was no bread. Get in the space, every time you blow, that’s the important thing.
